meta.description: Mirror active Claude skills into Codex

user.t:
Side task (this prompt is your spec). The user chose to make ALL currently-active Claude Code plugin skills available in OpenAI Codex CLI (codex-cli 0.161.0, config at C:/Users/mariu/.codex, user skills dir C:/Users/mariu/.codex/skills currently empty).

Build a re-runnable mirror tool in a NEW folder C:/Users/mariu/ai-tooling/codex-skill-mirror (git init locally; commit with the Co-Authored-By trailer; never push). Do not modify anything under C:/Users/mariu/.claude except reading. Do not edit C:/Users/mariu/.codex/config.toml.

1. First establish Codex's real skill format and limits from Codex's own installed files/docs (look in C:/Users/mariu/AppData/Roaming/npm/node_modules/@openai/codex/ and C:/Users/mariu/.codex/vendor_imports, C:/Users/mariu/.codex/plugins/* for examples of SKILL.md layout, frontmatter fields, name/description length limits, name character rules, how many skills it loads, whether nested folders are scanned). Run `codex --help` / `codex features list` etc. if useful. Record findings in README.
2. Determine the ACTIVE plugin set exactly as Claude Code does: plugins under C:/Users/mariu/.claude/plugins/synced/*/* and C:/Users/mariu/.claude/plugins/cache/*/*/* whose name@synced / name@<marketplace> is NOT set to false in C:/Users/mariu/.claude/settings.json enabledPlugins (note: context7 and superpowers were just enabled — their entries were removed). Dedupe plugins by name (prefer highest version / most components).
3. For each active plugin's skills/<skill>/SKILL.md: copy the whole skill folder to ~/.codex/skills/<plugin>--<skill>/ (sanitise to Codex's name rules), rewrite frontmatter `name` to that unique name (keep description; truncate to Codex's limit if any, append "(from Claude plugin <plugin>)"), and replace occurrences of ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} / $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT in copied text files with the plugin's absolute directory so bundled scripts still resolve. Preserve disable-model-invocation semantics if Codex has an equivalent; otherwise note it in the description ("user-invoked only"). Skip skills whose files fail to parse, and report them.
4. Write a manifest (~/.codex/skills/.claude-mirror-manifest.json) listing everything the tool created, so re-runs update/remove ONLY mirror-owned folders (never touch other user skills). Support --dry-run, --plugin <name> filter, and --remove-all.
5. Safety: never copy [SENSITIVE_PATH][SENSITIVE_PATH]/*.key files; skip symlinks pointing outside the plugin; cap per-skill folder size (e.g. 20 MB) and report skipped; do not execute any plugin code.
6. Run it for real, then report: count of skills mirrored, skipped (with reasons), total size, Codex limits found, whether Codex actually lists them (verify with a non-interactive codex command if one exists that lists skills; do not start an interactive session or call a model), and the expected context impact in Codex (honest: thousands of skill descriptions may exceed Codex's skill-list budget too).
Tests (node:test) for name sanitising, manifest-only removal, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} rewrite, secret-file exclusion.

handback.t:
I built the mirror tool, ran it for real, and 3,024 Claude plugin skills are now in `~/.codex/skills`. But this makes Codex worse, not better. Codex loads only 1,999 of them, shows the model 224 names with no descriptions at all, and has dropped its own skills (documents, pdf, presentations, spreadsheets and others) from what the model sees. To undo it: `node C:/Users/mariu/ai-tooling/codex-skill-mirror/bin/codex-skill-mirror.mjs --remove-all`. I left the mirror in place because the task said to run it for real; you or the user decide whether to keep it, roll it back, or mirror a small subset.

The 19 unit tests pass on Node 24 and on Node 22.23.3; one more symlink test is skipped because creating symlinks needs admin rights here, and the same case is covered with a junction. A second run reported all 3,024 unchanged, and `--dry-run` writes nothing. One local commit, `47a0c20`, not pushed. Nothing under `~/.claude` was written and `~/.codex/config.toml` was not touched. There was no StatsClaw run directory for this side task, so I wrote no implementation.md and made no mailbox.md entry.

**The run**
- **Plugins:** 675 active after removing 116 duplicate directories; 984 directories are disabled in `enabledPlugins`. superpowers is included (15 skills). context7 has no skills folder, so nothing came from it.
- **Mirrored:** 3,024 skills, 105.1 MB of content (144 MB on disk).
  - 128 are marked user-invoked only, using Codex's equivalent of `disable-model-invocation` (a setting that hides them from the model but keeps `$name` invocation).
  - 1,728 `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`-style references were replaced with the plugin's real path.
- **Skipped whole skills:** none. No skill failed to parse and none was over the 20 MB cap.
- **Frontmatter added:** 16 skills had no frontmatter at all. Claude Code loads these, Codex can't, so I gave them one using the folder name and first paragraph rather than skipping them. They are mac-disk-cleaner (2), memo-yoshi, notion-memory, private-credit (6), templatecentral (4) and trip-json.
- **Files left out inside mirrored skills:** three `[SENSITIVE_PATH]`/`[SENSITIVE_PATH]` files (anson, two in streaming-skills-plugin), excluded as secrets to be safe. Two `.cursor-plugin/` folders (blaxel); with those present Codex renamed the skills to `blaxel-cli:blaxel--…`, which I confirmed in a test.
- **Nested `SKILL.md` files:** 40 (in opensearch-skills and datarobot) were renamed to `SKILL.nested.md` and the links to them rewritten. Otherwise Codex would load them as extra skills with bare names like `cloud`.

**Codex limits I found (Codex 0.161.0)**
- **Names:** at most 64 characters. Codex's own skill validator also wants only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens with no `--`, but the loader accepts `--`, so I kept the `<plugin>--<skill>` naming you specified.
- **Descriptions:** capped at 1,024 characters.
- **Extra frontmatter keys:** ignored, not an error.
- **Folder depth:** subfolders are scanned about 6 levels deep.
- **How many skills load:** about 2,000 per skills folder, taken alphabetically. In a test with 2,500 skills, 1,999 loaded.
- **Context budget:** the skill list Codex puts in front of the model is limited (`skills.max_context_tokens`). When it overflows, Codex strips every description, including its own skills', then cuts the list.

**What Codex actually shows** (checked with `codex app-server` `skills/list` and `codex debug prompt-input`; neither starts a session or calls a model)
- 1,999 of the 3,024 mirrored skills load, with no load errors. Everything from `ruflo-adr--…` onward alphabetically does not load, including the ruflo plugins that are explicitly enabled.
- The model-visible list grew from 11 skills with descriptions (about 1.2k tokens) to 228 entries with no descriptions (about 5.4k tokens).
- Overriding `skills.max_context_tokens` only raised the list to 424 entries, still without descriptions.
- I couldn't confirm that `$name` invocation works for the loaded skills: `debug prompt-input` doesn't expand `$` mentions even for Codex's own skills.

**Recommendation:** the list holds roughly 21–22k characters, so about 40–50 mirrored skills with descriptions fit. Mirror a hand-picked subset with `--plugin a --plugin b …` (also accepts a comma list), or shrink the active set in Claude's `enabledPlugins`. The tool prints a warning when the total goes over about 2,000.

**How the tool keeps it safe**
- **Manifest:** `C:/Users/mariu/.codex/skills/.claude-mirror-manifest.json`, plus a `.claude-mirror.json` marker in each mirrored folder.
- **Ownership:** a folder is only updated or removed if it is in the manifest and has a matching marker. An existing folder with the same name is left alone and reported as a conflict.
- **Exclusions:** secret-like files are never copied, links pointing outside the plugin are skipped, and nothing from the plugins is executed.
- **Tests:** they cover the four areas you asked for (name sanitising, manifest-only removal, plugin-path rewriting, secret-file exclusion), plus discovery, dry-run, re-run and `--plugin`.
- **Findings:** the README records the Codex limits and the before/after measurements.

Files are in C:/Users/mariu/ai-tooling/codex-skill-mirror:
- README.md
- bin/codex-skill-mirror.mjs
- scripts/verify-codex.mjs
- src/names.mjs
- src/frontmatter.mjs
- src/discover.mjs
- src/copy.mjs
- src/mirror.mjs
- test/names.test.mjs
- test/copy.test.mjs
- test/mirror.test.mjs
